arxiv-2011-14342.title: Extreme Parametric Sensitivity in the Steady-State Photoisomerization of Two-Dimensional Model Rhodopsin
arxiv-2011-14342.creator: Chern Chuang, Paul Brumer
arxiv-2011-14342.description: Abstract We computationally studied the photoisomerization reaction of the retinal chromophore in rhodopsin using a two-state two-mode model coupled to thermal baths. Reaction quantum yields at the steady state (10 ps and beyond) were found to be considerably different than their transient values, suggesting a weak correlation between transient and steady-state dynamics in these systems.

arxiv-2302-00843.title: Computational Dualism and Objective Superintelligence
arxiv-2302-00843.creator: Michael Timothy Bennett
arxiv-2302-00843.description: Abstract The concept of intelligent software is flawed. The behaviour of software is determined by the hardware that “interprets” it. This undermines claims regarding the behaviour of theorised, software superintelligence. Here we characterise this problem as “computational dualism”, where instead of mental and physical substance, we have software and hardware.

arxiv-2405-16505.title: He-enriched starevol models for globular cluster multiple populations
arxiv-2405-16505.creator: G. Costa, T. Dumont, A. Lançon, A. Palacios, C. Charbonnel, P. Prugniel, S. Ekstrom, C. Georgy, V. Branco, P. Coelho, L. Martins, S. Borisov, K. Voggel, W. Chantereau
arxiv-2405-16505.description: Abstract A common property of globular clusters (GCs) is to host multiple populations characterized by peculiar chemical abundances. Recent photometric studies suggest that the He content could vary between the populations of a GC by up to Δ \Delta He ∼ \sim 0.13, in mass fraction.

arxiv-2510-25706.title: Cosmological Constraints from Dark Energy Survey Year 1 Cluster Lensing and Abundances with Simulation-based Forward-modeling
arxiv-2510-25706.creator: Andrés N. Salcedo, Eduardo Rozo, Hao-Yi Wu, David H. Weinberg, Pranav Chiploonkar, Chun-Hao To, Shulei Cao, Eli S. Rykoff, Nicole Marcelina Gountanis, Conghao Zhou
arxiv-2510-25706.description: Abstract We present a simulation-based forward-modeling framework for cosmological inference from optical galaxy-cluster samples, and apply it to the abundance and weak-lensing signals of DES-Y1 redMaPPer clusters. The model embeds cosmology-dependent optical selection using a counts-in-cylinders approach, while also accounting for cluster miscentering and baryonic feedback in lensing.

arxiv-2512-05513.title: Know-Show: Benchmarking Video-Language Models on Spatio-Temporal Grounded Reasoning
arxiv-2512-05513.creator: Chinthani Sugandhika, Chen Li, Deepu Rajan, Basura Fernando
arxiv-2512-05513.description: Abstract Large Video-Language Models (Video-LMs) have achieved impressive progress in multimodal understanding, yet their reasoning remains weakly grounded in space and time. We present Know-Show, a new benchmark designed to evaluate spatio-temporal grounded reasoning, the ability of a model to reason about actions and their semantics while simultaneously grounding its inferences in visual and temporal evidence.

arxiv-2601-01271.description: Abstract Exception handling is a vital forward error-recovery mechanism in many programming languages, enabling developers to manage runtime anomalies through structured constructs (e.g., try-catch blocks). Improper or missing exception handling often leads to severe consequences, including system crashes and resource leaks.

pmc-10535904.title: Incorporation of Chitosan in Polyurethanes Based on Modified Castor Oil for Cardiovascular Applications
pmc-10535904.creator: Maria Morales-González, Kelly Navas-Gómez, Luis E Diaz, José A Gómez-Tejedor, Manuel F Valero, Zilu Wang
pmc-10535904.description: The increased demand for vascular grafts for the treatment of cardiovascular diseases has led to the search for novel biomaterials that can achieve the properties of the tissue. According to this, the investigation of polyurethanes has been a promising approach to overcome the present limitations. However, some biological properties remain to be overcome, such as thrombogenicity and hemocompatibility, among others.

pmc-10675484.title: Characterization and Pharmacokinetic Assessment of a New Berberine Formulation with Enhanced Absorption In Vitro and in Human Volunteers
pmc-10675484.creator: Julia Solnier, Yiming Zhang, Yun Chai Kuo, Min Du, Kyle Roh, Roland Gahler, Simon Wood, Chuck Chang
pmc-10675484.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Berberine is a plant-origin quaternary isoquinoline alkaloid with a vast array of biological activities, including antioxidant and blood-glucose- and blood-lipid-lowering effects. However, its therapeutic potential is largely limited by its poor oral bioavailability. The aim of this study was to investigate the in vitro solubility and Caco-2 cell permeability followed by pharmacokinetic profiling in healthy volunteers of a new food-grade berberine delivery system (i.e., Berberine LipoMicel®).

pmc-11312179.title: Effects of High-Hydrostatic-Pressure Treatment on Polyphenols and Volatile Aromatic Compounds in Marselan Wine
pmc-11312179.creator: Zicheng Yi, Danqing Zhao, Tengwen Chang, Xiang Chen, Jianrong Kai, Yang Luo, Bangzhu Peng, Binkun Yang, Qian Ge
pmc-11312179.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This study investigated the effects of high-hydrostatic-pressure (HHP) treatment of varying intensity (100–600 MPa) and duration (10–30 min) on polyphenols and volatile aromatic compounds in Marselan red wine. The types and concentrations of polyphenols and volatile aromatic compounds were compared before and after HHP treatment; the results indicated that HHP treatment at 300 MPa for 20 min significantly increased the total polyphenol content to 369.70 mg/L, a rise of 35.82%.

pmc-11384198.creator: Katharina Hohlbaum, Niek Andresen, Paul Mieske, Pia Kahnau, Benjamin Lang, Kai Diederich, Rupert Palme, Lars Mundhenk, Henning Sprekeler, Olaf Hellwich, Christa Thöne-Reineke, Lars Lewejohann, Jesse D Cushman, Jesse D Cushman, Katharina Hohlbaum, Rasneer Sonia Bains, Katharina Hohlbaum
pmc-11384198.description: BackgroundDue to the lack of complexity and variety of stimuli, conventional housing conditions of laboratory mice do not allow these animals to fully express their behavioral repertoire, including manipulative and cognitive activities. Therefore, we designed mechanical puzzles, so-called lockboxes, for mice that can be provided in their home cages.

pmc-11404821.title: The impact of COVID-19 on smoking cessation services with insights for post-pandemic delivery
pmc-11404821.creator: Windi Lameck Marwa, Claire Griffiths, Sophie Edwards, Paul Gately, Caroline Marshall, Carlton Cooke
pmc-11404821.description: Smoking is a leading cause of preventable morbidity and mortality globally. During the COVID-19 pandemic, Smoking Cessation (SC) services faced many challenges, including lockdown and social distancing restrictions. Consequently, SC services had to adapt to the challenges in different ways or halt delivery. This research evaluated the impact of COVID-19 on the delivery and outcomes of SC services.

pmc-11641590.creator: Diane M. Tshikudi, Hannah Hutchison, Jean-Eric Ghia
pmc-11641590.description: The impaired mucosal barrier is a hallmark of ulcerative colitis (UC), an inflammatory colonic disorder with epidemiological and pathophysiology sex bias. UC Patients overexpress the colonic epithelial cells (CECs)-derived peptide pancreastatin (PST). Pancreastatin inhibitor 8 (PSTi8), an inhibitor of PST, has shown promising anti-inflammatory effects on UC. However, no data exist in the context of CEC barrier function and integrity.

pmc-12730778.title: The Use of Calcaneal Quantitative Ultrasound as a Bone Health Screening Tool Amongst People Living with HIV and Taking Tenofovir-Based Antiretroviral Therapy: A Pilot Study
pmc-12730778.creator: Wenjian Zhao, Muhamad Riduan Daud, Hashwin Singh Tejpal Singh, Sophia Ogechi Ekeuku, Xiong Khee Cheong, Najma Kori, Petrick Periyasamy, Kok-Yong Chin, Massimiliano Lanzafame
pmc-12730778.description: Background/Objectives: Individuals living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) receiving tenofovir-based antiretroviral therapy (ART) are at increased risk of bone loss. Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA), the gold standard for determining bone mineral density (BMD), has limited accessibility. Calcaneal quantitative ultrasound (QUS) is an alternative screening tool for bone health, but its performance needs validation.

pmc-13063327.title: The chain mediating role of emotion dysregulation and non-suicidal self-injury in the relationship between cyber-victimization and suicidal ideation among college students
pmc-13063327.creator: Meng Gao, Chunfen Zhou, Jing Diao, Chen Liu, Xinxin Zhang, Haixing Wang, Hongmei Liu, Ying Lei
pmc-13063327.description: ObjectiveCyber-victimization has been increasingly linked to suicidal ideation, yet the underlying psychological mechanisms remain underexplored among college students. This study examined the relationship between cyber-victimization and suicidal ideation among Chinese college students, with a focus on the mediating roles of emotion dysregulation and non-suicidal self-injury.MethodA total of 2001 students aged 18–24 completed questionnaires.

pmc-13579796.title: Gene co-expression networks related to intramuscular fatty acid composition across different pig genotypes
pmc-13579796.creator: Mariah Castro Durval, Luiz F. Brito, Simara Larissa Fanalli, Fernanda Nery Ciconello, Camila Sabino Oliveira, Lucas Echevarria Nascimento, Bruna Pereira Martins da Silva, Aline Silva Mello Cesar
pmc-13579796.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThe nutritional quality of pork, a vital source of protein in the human diet, is being increasingly studied due to health concerns regarding pork fatty acid (FA) composition. Therefore, the primary objective of this study was to identify the relationship between muscle gene expression and the composition of different FAs in pigs, focusing on the two prevalent genotypes (AA and AB) from hotspot expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) regions within the study population.
